 Welcome to the Marksmanship Hunter rotation guide for ! This guide will teach you all about the optimal rotation for Marksmanship Hunter across its various talent builds. It will cover both core ability cadence and cooldown usage in dungeons and raids for .

Basics

Marksmanship Hunter Rotation in 

The rotation for Marksmanship Hunter focuses on maximizing your use of certain buffs, and maximizing your number of uses of cooldown-limited abilities. Marksmanship has a fairly consistent flow, where one ability logically flows into the next, with a few priority shifts based on procs and buff uptimes.

Precise Shots: These procs are guaranteed to happen from all Aimed Shots, and, depending on Talents, Rapid Fire as well. They are spent on Arcane Shot on single-target and Multi-Shot on 2+ targets, at least when we play Trick Shots. Every single proc must be spent, and in practice, this boils down to simply following up every Aimed Shot/Rapid Fire with a Arcane Shot/Multi-Shot.

Bulletstorm: This buff is generated from casting Rapid Fire, and massively buffs your Aimed Shot. Rapid Fire does not do a great deal of damage on its own in most builds, so activating Bulletstorm to buff your Aimed Shots is often its primary purpose.

Movement: While not strictly a rotational concept, while the flow of Marksmanship is straightforward, managing your movement is a big part of mastering it. The core thing to remember is that you should try and reserve movement for when you are not casting Aimed Shot. Whenever you are not casting Aimed Shot, you can move freely without interrupting your rotation, and you should take advantage of this fact to always think "can I be positioned ever so slightly better" and to move accordingly. Standing still while not casting Aimed Shot is rarely the best move.

Marksmanship Hunter Starter Guide

 Best Marksmanship Hunter Rotation

Our rotation has a fairly simple priority structure, with a few nuances based on procs and buffs. There is a fairly consistent flow to the rotation, where one button leads into the next, and there are not many decisions to make outside of "do I have this proc or buff".

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Marksmanship Hunter: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.

Hero Talent Master Switches

You can use the master switches below to flip the entire page's options to your selected choice.

]Dark Ranger

 Best Marksmanship Hunter Single Target Rotation

Marksmanship has a consistent flow to its rotation, where one button leads into the next in a logical way. The main times you will have to worry about the priority are when choosing how to prioritize abilities like Aimed Shot, Rapid Fire, and Moonlight Chakram, particularly when they are all active at the same time.

 With selected, the priority is as follows: With selected, the priority is as follows:

 Please select a Hero Talent
option to generate a Single Target priority 

The builds used below are covered in the Talents page. Anywhere you see the icon, you can hover over it for additional notes.

Priority

Trinket Usage We usually want to pair stat-granting on-use trinkets with Trueshot. Algeth'ar Puzzle Box should be used shortly before Trueshot; avoid spending time casting it after Trueshot has already been popped. Ideally, pair it with Rapid Fire as in the opener.
Cast Black Arrow as your primary Precise Shots spender. Always cast Black Arrow immediately after every Aimed Shot and Rapid Fire, provided you have a Black Arrow proc available.
Cast Aimed Shot if it is about to reach 2 charges.
During Trueshot, cast Aimed Shot if you have a Black Arrow proc available but no Precise Shots to spend it with.
Activate Trueshot, your major cooldown. We ideally press Trueshot right before we normally intend to Aimed Shot, and ideally, right or shortly after a Rapid Fire, so that you carry a fresh Bulletstorm into your cooldowns. It is extremely important that you never cast Trueshot and Volley back-to-back in any order, to avoid wasting Double Tap. Always fire, ideally, an Aimed Shot between them.
Cast Rapid Fire on cooldown.
Cast Wailing Arrow if you do not have a Black Arrow proc available.
Cast Arcane Shot as a backup Precise Shots spender if Black Arrow is not available.
Cast Volley on cooldown. On single-target, its main role is doing a bit of damage for us, while activating Double Tap. Never cast Volley directly before or after Trueshot, as that wastes the Double Tap generated by either.
Cast Aimed Shot.
Cast Explosive Shot.
Cast Steady Shot as a filler. Do not overlook the importance of filling every "empty" moment with these, as they generate significant Focus and Aimed Shot cooldown reduction.

The builds used below are covered in the Talents page. Anywhere you see the icon, you can hover over it for additional notes.

Priority

Trinket Usage We usually want to pair stat-granting on-use trinkets with Trueshot. Algeth'ar Puzzle Box should be used shortly before Trueshot; avoid spending time casting it after Trueshot has already been popped. Ideally, pair it with Rapid Fire as in the opener.
Cast Volley on cooldown. On single-target, its main role is doing a bit of damage for us, while activating Double Tap. On 1 target, cast Volley into Rapid Fire before Trueshot if both are available; otherwise, just press Volley on cooldown. On 2+ targets, Volley is used on an Aimed Shot inside Trueshot. Never hold Volley for Trueshot or vice versa. Never cast Volley directly before or after Trueshot, as that wastes the Double Tap generated by either.
Activate Trueshot, your major cooldown. We ideally press Trueshot right before we normally intend to Aimed Shot, and ideally, right or shortly after a Rapid Fire, so that you carry a fresh Bulletstorm into your cooldowns. It is extremely important that you never cast Trueshot and Volley back-to-back in any order, to avoid wasting Double Tap. Always fire, ideally, an Aimed Shot between them.
Cast Aimed Shot if it is about to reach 2 charges.
Cast Rapid Fire if Bulletstorm is either down, or would expire before your next Aimed Shot, or regardless if your target is below 20% HP.
Spend the Precise Shots stacks generated by Aimed Shot and Rapid Fire. Your PS spender priority is: Kill Shot > Arcane Shot for single-target. If there are 2 targets+ up, skip Kill Shot. During Trueshot, Arcane Shot can only be cast immediately after an Aimed Shot — never as a follow-up to Rapid Fire, Volley, or anything else.
Cast Moonlight Chakram if Trueshot has fewer than 3 seconds remaining, to guarantee you get a Chakram cast inside the window.
Cast Aimed Shot.
Cast Moonlight Chakram as a filler. You never want to let it lapse.
Cast Rapid Fire.
Cast Explosive Shot.
Cast Steady Shot as a filler. Do not overlook the importance of filling every "empty" moment with these, as they generate significant Focus and Aimed Shot cooldown reduction.

 Best Marksmanship Hunter AoE Rotation

The primary change for AoE is simply replacing Arcane Shot with Multi-Shot, at least while we run Trick Shots Talent, which we do not always do. While Trick Shots is a core and crucial mechanic when we run the talent, it actually takes care of itself, because it is generated from Multi-Shot, a button that we already press to spend our Precise Shots procs. It is essential that we never cast Aimed Shot or Rapid Fire without the Trick Shots buff, but by just following the same principles as our single-target rotation of always following up all of our Aimed Shots and Rapid Fires with a Multi-Shot, we will always have Trick Shots uptime without needing to think about it at all.

Without Trick Shots, i.e when running Aspect of the Hydra, the AoE rotation is identical to the Single-Target rotation. Refer to the Sentinel Single-Target Priority above and follow it for AoE scenarios as well. Aspect of the Hydra's cleaving handles multi-target damage naturally within that priority. The rotation below assumes you are running Trick Shots.

Cast Aimed Shot.
Cast Multi-Shot with Precise Shots.
Cast Explosive Shot if specced, which it typically isn't.
Cast Steady Shot as a filler. Do not overlook the importance of filling every "empty" moment with these, as they generate significant Focus and Aimed Shot cooldown reduction.

Spend the Precise Shots stacks generated by Aimed Shot and Rapid Fire by using Multi-Shot. You should also use it to activate Trick Shots if it is down, regardless of other conditions.
Cast Rapid Fire if Bulletstorm is either down, or would expire before your next Aimed Shot, or regardless, if your target is below 20% HP.

With Shrapnel Shot talented, cast Explosive Shot outside of Trueshot and when you do not already have a Lock and Load proc, to give yourself one, if Aimed Shot has 1 or fewer charges available.
Cast Aimed Shot whenever possible.
Cast Moonlight Chakram when you have no Aimed Shots remaining, or if Trueshot is about to run out.
Cast Rapid Fire with Trick Shots.
Cast Explosive Shot.

Best Marksmanship Hunter Opener

Our opener seeks to get the cooldowns of our core abilities rolling and setting up a strong Trueshot to start off the fight. There is not much "special" to be said about it, we are really just pursuing the priorities of our base rotation under the unique constraints (or lack thereof) of having absolutely everything available at the start of the fight. The main thing to note is that you want to pre-cast your first Aimed Shot about 2.5 seconds before combat starts, so that it hits right as combat starts and effectively "saves" you that time in combat.

Pre-Combat Check

Before any combat happens, it is important for Marksmanship Hunter to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

 Marksmanship Hunter Major Cooldowns

Marksmanship only has one cooldown of note, Trueshot. It has almost no impact on our rotation, with most of its value being in its crit chance and crit damage buff. It does also speed up our Aimed Shot and Rapid Fire cooldowns, but this does not impact our rotational priorities, and is more of a "nice to have" rather than something that we build our rotation around.

 Trueshot 

Trueshot massively increases our critical strike chance, damage, and the cooldown rates of Aimed Shot and Rapid Fire, as well as Aimed Shot's cast time. It makes us do everything stronger and faster.

Our rotational priorities are the same inside of Trueshot as they are outside of it. The main way we think about it is how we set up for it. The best use of our time, and our greatest damaging ability that we want Trueshot to amplify, is Aimed Shot. For this reason, a good rule of thumb is to activate Trueshot right before an Aimed Shot comes up in your rotation naturally.

Another good rule of thumb is to come into the Trueshot window with Bulletstorm already active with a healthy duration. For this reason, we like to cast Rapid Fire right before entering Trueshot, letting us focus as much of our time as possible on heavily buffed Aimed Shot.

For , activating Trueshot also gives us a Black Arrow proc, which we need to activate Precise Shots before we can fire.

For both Hero Talents, activating Trueshot turns the Trueshot button into another ability: Moonlight Chakram for , and Wailing Arrow for . These abilities have one use only and should be used as a "filler" in your cooldowns, at a time where they would not interfere with your other rotational priorities.

 Marksmanship Hunter Advanced Tips

You could argue that it is a basic tip, but it is still the #1 issue that even "good" Marksmanship Hunters face, and it is to ensure that you are always casting something. Marksmanship always has something to cast, because even if you run out of absolutely every resource and cooldown, you can always Steady Shot, and within 2 seconds, you are back to casting Aimed Shot.

 Always Be Casting 

The problem is not so much that people forget that Steady Shot exists, however. It is understanding the value of time in the DPS equation. Most people press their buttons rather slowly, they press buttons that are not available to them, their DPS rotation stops when they are focused on a mechanic, or they just have bad reaction times. All of these things lead to lost time where you are not casting anything, often for very small windows of time, but these small windows of time add up very quickly, and they are the difference between a good and a great player. Always be casting something, even if it is just Steady Shot, and you will see a noticeable increase in your DPS.

Our Marksmanship Hunter guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on View Changelog in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Marksmanship Hunter guides for , make sure to browse the Navigation Bar at the top of the page, along with our list of Related Guides just beneath the Table of Contents.

With Aimed Shot having 2 charges, we are fine to leave it unused at 1 charge since its cooldown is still regenerating. What we don't want is for it to ever reach 2 charges, because then its cooldown is not ticking. This is why we are happy to prioritize Rapid Fire over it when it only has 1 charge, but not two.

Utilizing your cooldowns as they become available, timing them with other cooldowns, and overlapping properly.
Following the Assisted Combat suggestions exactly, or only pressing the Single-Button without any other buttons being used.

actions.sentaoe+=/volley,if=!buff.double_tap.up
actions.sentaoe+=/explosive_shot,if=talent.shrapnel_shot&buff.trueshot.down&buff.lock_and_load.down&cooldown.aimed_shot.charges_fractional<=1.1
actions.sentaoe+=/aimed_shot,target_if=max:debuff.sentinels_mark.up|max_prio_damage,if=buff.trick_shots.remains>cast_time
actions.sentaoe+=/moonlight_chakram
actions.sentaoe+=/rapid_fire,if=buff.trick_shots.remains>execute_time
actions.sentaoe+=/multishot,target_if=max:debuff.spotters_mark.down|action.aimed_shot.in_flight_to_target|max_prio_damage,if=buff.precise_shots.up&talent.windrunner_quiver
actions.sentaoe+=/explosive_shot
actions.sentaoe+=/steady_shot

actions.sentst=volley,if=!buff.double_tap.up
actions.sentst+=/trueshot,if=!buff.double_tap.up&variable.trueshot_ready
actions.sentst+=/rapid_fire,if=buff.bulletstorm.stack<18
actions.sentst+=/aimed_shot,target_if=max:debuff.sentinels_mark.up|max_prio_damage,if=full_recharge_time<gcd+cast_time
actions.sentst+=/arcane_shot,target_if=max:debuff.sentinels_mark.down|action.aimed_shot.in_flight_to_target|max_prio_damage,if=buff.precise_shots.up&(buff.trueshot.up&prev_gcd.1.aimed_shot|!buff.trueshot.up)
actions.sentst+=/rapid_fire,if=(buff.bulletstorm.remains<action.aimed_shot.execute_time|talent.unload&target.health.pct<20)
actions.sentst+=/kill_shot,target_if=max:debuff.sentinels_mark.down|action.aimed_shot.in_flight_to_target|max_prio_damage,if=buff.precise_shots.up&active_enemies=1
actions.sentst+=/moonlight_chakram,if=buff.trueshot.remains<execute_time+gcd
actions.sentst+=/aimed_shot,target_if=max:debuff.sentinels_mark.up|max_prio_damage
actions.sentst+=/moonlight_chakram
actions.sentst+=/rapid_fire
actions.sentst+=/explosive_shot
actions.sentst+=/steady_shot

# A buff trinket that lines up cleanly with Trueshot; use with Trueshot.
actions.trinkets=use_items,check_existing=0,slots=trinket1:trinket2,if=this_trinket.has_use_buff&this_trinket.cooldown.duration%%cooldown.trueshot.duration=0&(buff.trueshot.remains>14|this_trinket.is.algethar_puzzle_box&variable.trueshot_ready&cooldown.trueshot.remains<5)

# A buff trinket paired with a trinket that matches the above line; use with Trueshot if the other trinket is not ready or use without Trueshot if the other trinket will come up for the next Trueshot.
actions.trinkets+=/use_items,check_existing=0,slots=trinket1:trinket2,if=this_trinket.has_use_buff&other_trinket.has_use_buff&other_trinket.cooldown.duration%%cooldown.trueshot.duration=0&(buff.trueshot.remains>14&other_trinket.cooldown.remains|cooldown.trueshot.remains>20&other_trinket.cooldown.remains<=cooldown.trueshot.remains)

# A buff trinket, use with Trueshot or in the last ~20 seconds of the fight.
actions.trinkets+=/use_items,check_existing=0,slots=trinket1:trinket2,if=this_trinket.has_use_buff&(buff.trueshot.remains>14|buff.trueshot.up&fight_remains<cooldown.trueshot.remains+15|fight_remains<21)

# A damage trinket; use when Trueshot has at least 20 seconds remaining on its cooldown.
actions.trinkets+=/use_items,check_existing=0,slots=trinket1:trinket2,if=this_trinket.has_use_damage&cooldown.trueshot.remains>20
